findings.title: findMany method removed without updating callers
findings.body: The `findMany` method that previously executed the authorization/filter query through `prisma.bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany` has been removed and replaced by `getBaseConditions()` plus a `prisma.$queryRaw` interpolation. The integration test was migrated to the new shape, but no other callers are updated in this PR. If any HTTP route, tRPC procedure, scheduled job, or other service in the repository invokes `InsightsBookingService.findMany(...)`, those call sites will now fail to compile and/or at runtime. Either the call sites must be migrated in this PR or a transitional shim should be added so the change is non-breaking.

findings.title: Org scope silently drops direct org members when there are no child teams
findings.body: In `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition`, `userIdsFromOrg` is set to `[]` whenever `teamsFromOrg.length === 0`, so the `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds` query is skipped entirely. `teamIds` already contains `options.orgId`, but the conditional means a user who is a direct member of the organization (membership row with `teamId = orgId`) but is not a member of any sub-team is never included. Their individual bookings (and any event-type-owned bookings they make) will be invisible in org-scope insights. The query should be executed unconditionally (or fall back to a direct membership lookup on `orgId`). The bug pre-existed in the WhereInput form but is reproduced verbatim in the new SQL, and the new tests do not cover the no-sub-teams case.

findings.title: Org-scope test depends on undefined query/Set ordering
findings.body: The org-scope assertion compares against literal array orderings `[testData.org.id, testData.team.id, team2.id, team3.id]` and `[testData.user.id, user2.id, user3.id]`. These come from `TeamRepository.findAllByParentId`, `MembershipRepository.findAllByTeamIds`, and `Array.from(new Set(userIdsFromOrg))`. None of those queries specify `ORDER BY`, so the order is implementation-defined and can vary across PostgreSQL versions, under concurrent load, or with different planner settings. A `toEqual` on `Prisma.sql` template literals compares the embedded `.values` arrays by deep equality, so any reorder will fail the test. Either add deterministic ordering on the repository queries, or normalize both sides of the assertion (e.g. compare by `Set` membership, or use a helper that re-sorts the array values) so the test is not order-sensitive.

findings.title: Invalid-options test bypasses TypeScript via `null as any`
findings.body: The constructor parameter is declared `options: InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` (required, non-null), but the test for "invalid options" passes `options: null as any` and relies on `safeParse` returning `{ success: false }` so `this.options` ends up `null` and `NOTHING_CONDITION` is produced. This hides a real design question: invalid options silently turn the caller into an unauthorized principal instead of throwing, which means a production bug that constructs an `InsightsBookingService` with a malformed `options` object would just return no data rather than fail loudly. The constructor should either throw on invalid input, or its type should be widened to `InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions | null | undefined` so callers can express intent without resorting to `as any`. The current arrangement also means the runtime contract is weaker than the type signature suggests.
